# Colophon and Changelog {#sec-97-colophon}



This appendix records what the book was built with, so that a reader who wants
to reproduce a number knows which versions produced it, and what has changed
between editions of the text.

## How This Book Was Built {#sec-97-colophon-built}

The book is a Quarto project. Every chapter is a `.qmd` file whose code runs
when the book is rendered, so every number, table and figure in the text is the
output of the code shown beside it. Results are cached with Quarto's freeze
mechanism and re-executed only when a chapter's source changes. The chapters run
from the project root and share one setup file, `R/_common.R`, which fixes the
random seed, the display options and the figure theme.

:::

The full dependency set, 299 packages in all, is pinned
in `renv.lock`; `renv::restore()` recreates it. Two dependencies do not come
from CRAN: `tidypm`, the companion package, which ships the modeled market
and the machinery `PortfolioAnalytics` does not have; and the build of
`PortfolioAnalytics` itself, which is the CRAN release with five fixes carried
on a fork while their pull requests are open. @sec-93-package-notes records every
deviation.

The data are the modeled market at dataset version 6.2.0, on its model
calendar of thirty-one model years, described in
@sec-02-notation-and-data-simulated-market and in full in
@sec-90-data-description. The dataset is frozen: the source model redraws the
idiosyncratic component of every instrument on each run, so a regenerated
dataset is a different realized path, and every number in the book is pinned
to this one. `R/verify-claims.R` in the repository recomputes the load-bearing
numbers and names the ones a new dataset would move.

The prose follows the conventions of *Tidy Finance with R* [@scheuch2023] and
*Machine Learning for Factor Investing* [@coqueret2020]: the question first,
the mathematics in the running text, the method attributed on first use, the
code executed, and takeaways and exercises at the end. The typeface is Source
Sans 3; the accent color is a light blue. Figures are drawn with `ggplot2` and
the theme in `R/_common.R`, and are built from a single data frame per figure
so that no coordinate can be paired with the wrong label.

## Review Status {#sec-97-colophon-status}

The book is reviewed in four stages, and every numbered chapter shows its
stage in the banner under its title: *draft* while it waits for the author's
read, *alpha* while two or three colleagues check the theory, the literature
and whether the chapter teaches, *beta* while readers in the student's seat
work it with its exercises, and *final* when they have been through it. The stages, the questions each reader is asked and what happens to a
comment are in the repository's `REVIEWING.md`; the status itself is one line
per chapter in `review/status.csv`, read here.

no obligation beyond the copyright notice. This is the arrangement of *Tidy
Finance with R* [@scheuch2023], whose example the book follows in this as in
its form.

## Citing This Book {#sec-97-colophon-cite}

The online edition is the edition of record, and the version is the date of
the render shown on each page. The repository carries a `CITATION.cff`; in
BibTeX:


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
```bibtex
@book{stoeckl2026tidyaa,
  author = {Stöckl, Sebastian},
  title  = {Tidy Asset Allocation in {R}},
  year   = {2026},
  url    = {https://www.tidy-pm.com/dev/},
  note   = {Online edition, version of 11 November 2026}
}
```
:::


## Changelog {#sec-97-colophon-changelog}

- **2026-11-11.** The build of `PortfolioAnalytics` moved to the fork head
  that carries all five open pull requests. The review machinery was set up:
  annotations on the page, a discussion thread under it, a review status per
  chapter, and the reviewers' guide. The code of every chapter became a
  download, with the exercises as a file and the solutions beside them, and
  @sec-966-teaching added three course plans.

- **2026-11-09.** The data moved to dataset version 6.2.0, read out of the
  source model itself, and onto a model calendar: thirty-one model years, with
  the stress episodes named for what happens in them. Every chapter was
  re-executed against it and its sentences checked against their numbers;
  chapters 18 and 19 were written.
- **2026-09-14.** The modeled market moved to export 5.1.0 and the class
  universe was fixed at the sixteen risky series, with the money markets shipped
  beside it. Every chapter was written or rewritten to the present contract,
  the appendices were generated from the sources, and the bibliography was
  checked entry by entry against Crossref. This is the first complete baseline
  of the book.
- **2026-09-13.** Chapter 9 was rewritten as the reference chapter and reviewed;
  the review produced the rules on data preparation, dominance vocabulary and
  worked examples that the other chapters follow. The review round-trip through
  Word was set up.
- **2026-09-12.** The book was restructured into its present twenty-eight
  chapters and eight parts, the four-beat chapter form was retired in favor of
  theory, implementation and application, mathematics returned to the running
  text with proofs in an appendix, and the design was rebuilt on one accent
  color.
- **2026-08-27.** The data layer: the companion package, the tibble–`xts`
  boundary, and the first export of the simulated market.
- **2018–2024.** Earlier drafts, as *Tidy Portfoliomanagement in R*, from which
  parts of the present material descend; see @sec-98-acknowledgements.
